title: CRM Mobile iPad — Authentication and Login Flow
summary: The legacy CRM iPad app authenticates via Salesforce credentials with multi-factor verification. Users can connect to Production, Sandbox, or regional cloud environments (including a China-specific connection hosted on a .cn domain via a regional cloud provider). After credential entry, the app may prompt for Salesforce Authenticator approval or a numeric authentication code. First login triggers a full database synchronization for the selected territory.

login_sequence: Launch app from iPad home screen
If enterprise certificate trust prompt appears, navigate to Settings > General > Device Management to trust the developer
Choose connection environment (Production, Sandbox, or regional cloud)
Complete MFA verification (authenticator approval or numeric code)
Grant app permissions for listed items
Set a passcode for app unlock
Optionally enable biometric unlock (Touch ID or Face ID)
Select territory if multiple are available
Wait for full synchronization to complete
connection_environments: Sandbox — testing purposes only, not for daily work
Regional cloud (China) — for users in China mainland, Hong Kong, or Macao with matching iPad Language & Region settings; hosted on .cn domain
mfa_methods: Salesforce Authenticator push approval on mobile device
migration_considerations: Authentication relies on Salesforce platform credentials — migration to a new CRM requires re-provisioning user accounts
MFA configuration is tied to the Salesforce org, not the app
China-region connectivity is app-specific and must be re-evaluated for any replacement platform
Territory-scoped database download means first login per territory incurs significant sync time

title: CRM Mobile iPad — Passcode Policies and Biometric Authentication
summary: The legacy CRM iPad app supports two passcode types configured by an administrator: numeric (4-digit) and alpha-numeric (8+ characters). Both types enforce complexity rules to prevent weak codes. Biometric unlock (Touch ID and Face ID) can be enabled as a convenience layer on top of the passcode.

numeric_passcode_rules: No digit may be used more than two times (e.g., 1121 is invalid)
Consecutive sequences are not allowed (e.g., 1234 is invalid)
alphanumeric_passcode_rules: Must include at least one number, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, and one symbol
Consecutive sequences are not allowed (e.g., Abcd123! is invalid)
biometric_options: Touch ID — fingerprint authentication via iPad Home button
Face ID — facial recognition in portrait orientation
Both are optional, enabled during initial login or via Change Passcode
Passcode remains the fallback if biometric recognition fails
admin_controlled_settings: Passcode type (numeric vs. alpha-numeric) is admin-configured, not user-selectable
Biometric enablement is user-controlled once available
migration_considerations: Replacement platform must support equivalent passcode complexity enforcement
Admin-controlled passcode type is a compliance feature customers depend on
Biometric unlock is expected on both iPad and iPhone form factors
Forgot-passcode flow forces full logout and re-login with Salesforce credentials

title: CRM Mobile iPad — Database Synchronization Types and Behavior
summary: The legacy CRM iPad app uses an offline-first architecture with multiple synchronization modes: Full Sync (all metadata + data for a territory), Delta Sync (incremental changes), and Upload Only Sync (one-way push of transactions). Synchronization runs automatically over Wi-Fi and can be manually triggered. A configurable offline limit forces a full sync if the device has been disconnected too long.

sync_types.full_sync: Downloads all metadata and data for the selected territory; uploads transactions, logs, and statistics. Triggered on initial login, territory switch, or exceeding the configured days-offline limit. Also triggered by admin-set 'Force Full Sync' flag.
sync_types.delta_sync: Updates database schema if needed, downloads/uploads incremental changes, downloads list views. Runs on manual sync or when metadata changes are detected after unlocking the app. Can run in foreground or background.
sync_types.upload_only_sync: One-way from mobile to server — uploads transactions, logs, and statistics only. Triggered automatically after creating or modifying data. If no Wi-Fi, transactions queue until next sync attempt.

sync_indicators: Animated App Settings icon during background sync
Sync Progress Bar shows completion percentage during foreground sync
Red last-sync timestamp if more than 24 hours since last sync
database_management: View Database screen shows object name, column count, record count, not-synced count, and not-verified count
Database Optimize frees unused space in the offline database
Submit Database uploads the offline database for support investigation
Platform events tracked separately — not stored in local database, show sync transaction count instead
migration_considerations: Full sync on territory switch means data is territory-scoped — replacement must handle the same isolation model
Admin-controlled 'Force Full Sync' flag is a support tool used in production — must have equivalent
Background auto-sync after record save is expected behavior — users do not manually sync after every change
Submit Database for support is a critical production support feature

title: CRM Mobile iPad — Device Settings, Siri Integration, and App Updates
summary: The legacy CRM iPad app integrates with several iOS system features: GPS location services for proximity calculations, camera and photo library for attachments, microphone and speech recognition for voice search, Siri shortcuts for hands-free access, and push notifications for activity reminders. The app also supports dark mode, display density settings, and over-the-air updates for both the app binary and metadata.

ios_integrations.location_services: GPS for distance-to-account (Next Best Customer), map centering, and optional coordinate capture during presentations, signatures, or call submission. Can be configured to warn if GPS is off during signature capture.
ios_integrations.camera_and_photos: Camera access for capturing photos as record attachments. Photo library access (full or limited) for attaching existing images.
ios_integrations.microphone_and_speech: Microphone for Remote Engagement audio and speech-to-text in search fields. Speech Recognition permission required separately.
ios_integrations.siri_shortcuts: Pre-built shortcuts: 'My Appointments for the Day' (Up Next list), 'Last Sync Time' (sync status), 'Unsubmitted Calls' (queue), 'Navigate to Next Appointment' (directions).
ios_integrations.notifications: Push notifications for planned activity reminders via iPad Notification Center.
ios_integrations.background_refresh: Background App Refresh for checking updates when app is not in foreground.

app_update_mechanisms: App Update — message prompts for new app version; can postpone with 'Later' or manually trigger via App Settings > Update App
Metadata Update — in-session prompt when server-side metadata changes; postpone triggers re-prompt later
New Build Available — install prompt for new build; cancel postpones until next app open

display_settings.dark_mode: Toggle via App Settings > Enable/Disable Dark Mode
display_settings.display_density: Comfy (more spacing) or Compact (condensed) — set in the online web application, synced to iPad after full sync
display_settings.locale_and_timezone: Set in Salesforce web app; requires logout/login or territory switch to apply in iPad app

migration_considerations: Siri shortcuts represent a differentiated user experience — replacement platform should offer equivalent voice automation
GPS capture during call submission is a compliance feature in some markets
Over-the-air metadata refresh without app store update is expected — silent config push is the norm
Dark mode and display density are expected features — not differentiators but table stakes

title: CRM Mobile iPad — Territory Management and Profile Settings
summary: The legacy CRM iPad app scopes all data to a single selected territory. Users with multiple territories can switch between them, triggering a full resynchronization. Managers can access their direct reports' territories. Profile settings including language, time zone, locale, and display density are managed via the Salesforce web application and require a sync to take effect on the device.

territory_behavior: Only one territory active at a time — all app data is scoped to the selected territory
Territory switch triggers upload of current territory data, then download of new territory data
Multi-level territory hierarchy supported — must select a leaf-level territory
Managers can view territories of their direct reports
profile_settings: Language and Time Zone changed via Salesforce web app (Settings > Language & Time Zone)
Locale setting drives Speech Recognition language in the iPad app
Time Zone setting used throughout the iPad app for scheduling and display
Changes require logout/login or territory switch to trigger full sync with updated metadata
additional_features: View Online — opens the Salesforce web application from within the iPad app
Provide Feedback — configurable in-app feedback mechanism with rating and text input; can be general or screen-specific
Help and Training link — admin-configurable link to an external help/training website, opens in app web viewer with navigation controls
migration_considerations: Territory-scoped data isolation is a fundamental design pattern — any replacement must support equivalent scoping
Manager territory access (viewing direct report territories) is used for field coaching workflows
Settings round-trip through the web app is a known friction point — opportunity for improvement in replacement
In-app feedback mechanism may be customer-specific and should be assessed for migration
